items.title: Iran-US-Israel war and hostilities
items.nowSummary: Iran's Nov 18 attacks on US-linked sites in Kuwait and Bahrain were intercepted; USS George Washington has left, two carriers remain; still no major-campaign order

items.headline: Iran attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain intercepted; ADNOC ship hit; UKMTO reports a Khasab tanker strike; George Washington leaves; coalition claims a Saada launcher destroyed
items.label: reported
changes: After a US strike on Qeshm, Iran launched drones at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait (the first strike on Kuwait since September) and at sites in Bahrain; Bahrain and Kuwait said the attacks were intercepted, with no damage reported.
ADNOC said one of its ships was struck in Hormuz on Nov 17: one crew member missing, 11 injured.
UKMTO reported an outbound tanker hit by an unknown projectile in the engine room north of Khasab, Oman; crew safe.
A Navy official told CBS the USS George Washington has left the Middle East for the 7th Fleet, leaving two carriers, the USS George H.W. Bush and USS Theodore Roosevelt.
The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a Houthi ballistic-missile launcher in Saada after an attempted attack on southern Saudi Arabia (coalition claim).

items.headline: Shenzhen summit yields no reported Iran breakthrough; Qatar mediation stalled; Saudi authorities report Houthi damage to a Riyadh tower; Houthis reported about 60 km from Aden
items.label: reported
changes: The Trump-Xi-Putin meeting in Shenzhen produced no reported Iran breakthrough, and Qatar's mediation remains stalled.

Saudi Civil Defense said a Houthi attack damaged several floors of a King Abdullah Financial District tower and adjacent buildings, with no injuries; the Foreign Ministry condemned the attack, the second KAFD hit after the Nov 8 Aramco Tower debris.
The Nov 19 PM update reported Houthis about 60 km from Aden and Yemeni government forces pulling back from Bab el-Mandeb.
NPR reported that ship attacks in Hormuz have escalated.

items.headline: Trump claims indications Iran may pursue chemical or biological weapons, citing no evidence; Iran rejects the claim; IRGC mine claims Unconfirmed; Houthi boat-toll claim unverified
items.label: claim_no_evidence_shown
changes: Trump told Fox on Nov 18-19, from Shenzhen, there are 'indications' Iran may be working on biological or chemical weapons because its nuclear program has been damaged; he cited no evidence.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Baqaei rejected the claim as the 'same fraudulent script' used about Iraq's weapons.
No supporting evidence has been shown; a denial is not a refutation.
The IRGC and Iran's navy said two more tankers hit mines near Hormuz on Nov 19 and caught fire, Iranian claims that have not been independently confirmed.
The Houthi health ministry said a Saudi strike on a civilian boat killed 19 people; that claim is unverified.

items.title: US strike decision on Iran
items.nowSummary: After a US strike on Qeshm, Iran launched drones at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait and at sites in Bahrain; official accounts say the attacks were intercepted, with no damage. Still no major-campaign order.

items.headline: Reuters: Trump told advisers he may hold off on renewed strikes unless Iran or the Houthis provoke further; no final decision (reported, not confirmed)
items.label: single_outlet
changes: Reuters, citing three people familiar with the matter, reported that Trump told advisers he may hold off on renewed strikes unless Iran or the Houthis take further provocative action; no final decision has been made (reported, not confirmed).
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkey's President Erdogan urged him not to resume attacks; Israel is still pressing for a new campaign.
Trump is expected to raise Iran with Putin and Xi at their Nov 19 summit.
